page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highcpu-4 is a compute-oriented virtual machine configuration built on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 4 dedicated virtual CPUs paired with 7.0 GB of system memory, yielding a ratio of 1.75 GB of RAM per vCPU. This allocation profile targets compute-dominant workloads where processing execution is prioritized over large resident memory sets.

The server includes no integrated local storage, requiring network-attached persistent disks for the base operating system and all persistent data. Hardware accelerators are absent, with zero GPUs included in the configuration. Additionally, complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not bundled with the instance, making external network routing dependent on supplementary cloud network configurations.

By maintaining a restrained memory allocation relative to its core count, c4d-highcpu-4 optimizes cost efficiency for compute-heavy workloads that do not consume large working memory. Tradeoffs include reliance on network storage latency and limited head-room for memory-intensive operations. The instance is suited for batch processing, continuous integration build runners, source compilation, and stateless web application serving.
